title: Radiation biology on the ANTARES external micro-beam irradiation facility at ANSTO
task: Establish ion microbeam facility for radiobiology research and validate DNA damage detection
key_results: Successfully detected DNA double-strand breaks (γH2AX foci) in human fibroblasts irradiated with MeV protons delivered through 75 nm silicon nitride membrane; demonstrated precise dose delivery with ion ranges up to 2 mm in water
comments: First operational microbeam radiobiology capability in Australia; technical validation study rather than novel biological discovery, but important infrastructure contribution for radiation research.

inputs: MeV-energetic ion beams (H, C, O, heavier ions)
cell culture on 75 nm silicon nitride membrane in culture media
outputs: Monte Carlo simulations of ion trajectories

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ion microbeam can deliver precise doses to live cells under ambient conditions and induce measurable DNA damage
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: γH2AX immunocytochemistry demonstrated successful DSB induction in irradiated fibroblasts

title: PKM2 AP: a micropeptide inhibits vascular calcification via molecular glue-mediated ubiquitination of PKM2
task: Identify and characterize micropeptide PKM2 AP as regulator of vascular calcification via PKM2 degradation
key_results: 40-amino acid PKM2 AP encoded by LINC01139 intron-retaining transcript acts as molecular glue promoting STUB1-mediated PKM2 ubiquitination and degradation; PKM2 degradation suppresses aerobic glycolysis and lactate, attenuating osteogenic transition; in vivo PKM2 AP administration and ORF2 knock-in alleviate vascular calcification in mouse models
comments: Novel micropeptide mechanism via molecular glue-mediated protein degradation; therapeutic relevance for CKD-associated vascular calcification is promising but requires further clinical validation.

model_io.model: mouse vascular calcification models; cultured vascular smooth muscle cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Micropeptide PKM2 AP suppresses vascular calcification by promoting PKM2 degradation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via molecular glue mechanism recruiting STUB1 E3 ligase and in vivo alleviation of calcification phenotypes

title: Combination of crocin and vitamin E mitigates UV-induced ROS and apoptosis in human skin fibroblasts
task: Evaluate synergistic cytoprotection of combined crocin and vitamin E against UV-induced ROS and apoptosis
key_results: Combined crocin + vitamin E showed synergistic reduction of intracellular/extracellular ROS and decreased apoptosis more effectively than either compound alone; improved cell viability through mitochondrial protection
comments: Study uses standard 2D fibroblast culture; acknowledged limitation that physiologically relevant 3D/tissue models needed for clinical translation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lipid- and water-soluble antioxidants act through complementary mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via synergistic ROS reduction and apoptosis inhibition in combination treatment

title: Targeting mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis in 5-fluorouracil–induced cardiotoxicity using kaempferol-mediated selenium nanoparticles
task: Evaluate cardioprotective mechanisms of kaempferol-selenium nanoparticles (KMP-SeNPs) against 5-FU-induced cardiotoxicity
key_results: KMP-SeNPs treatment significantly reduced cardiac injury markers, lipid peroxidation, and NO generation while restoring antioxidant defenses and increasing Nrf2 signaling; TNF-α, IL-6, NF-κB, Bax, and caspase-3 expression decreased, while IL-10, FOXP3, Bcl-2 increased, resulting in near-normal cardiac architecture by histopathology and immunohistochemistry
comments: Multi-targeted nanotherapeutic approach addressing oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis simultaneously; green synthesis and systemic administration suggest translational potential for cardioprotection during 5-FU chemotherapy.

hypotheses.hypothesis: KMP-SeNPs protect against 5-FU cardiotoxicity via antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via restoration of antioxidant defenses, suppression of pro-inflammatory/pro-apoptotic markers, and preservation of cardiac architecture

title: SOCS3 knockout of donor transplanted cells exacerbates GVHD associated with a high-fat diet in murine allogeneic HSCT
task: Determine role of donor SOCS3 deficiency and recipient high-fat diet in GVHD severity
key_results: SOCS3 KO donor + HFD recipient exacerbated GVHD with increased CD4/CD8 effector memory T cells, elevated IL-6 in recipient spleen (measured day 30 post-transplant), and shortened median survival vs. WT donor controls
comments: SOCS3 suppression of inflammation is context-dependent; metabolic stress from HFD synergizes with T cell dysregulation to worsen alloimmunity.

model_io.model: murine allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
inputs: SOCS3 KO or WT donor cells
high-fat diet or control diet in recipients
outputs: CD4+ and CD8+ T cell phenotypes

hypotheses.hypothesis: SOCS3 deficiency in donor cells and HFD in recipients synergistically worsen GVHD
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SOCS3 KO + HFD combination showed exacerbated disease vs. single perturbations

title: Autophagy-associated marker and stress-response changes in ASA- and 5-FU-treated 3D colorectal cancer spheroid models exposed to 3-MA or CQ
task: Evaluate interplay between autophagy inhibition/activation and drug-induced cell death in 3D colorectal cancer models
key_results: ASA + 5-FU combined with 3-MA and CQ showed treatment- and cell line-dependent changes in colonosphere size, ATP levels (marked reduction with ASA-containing conditions), autophagy markers (BECN1, LC3A/B, SQSTM1), and caspase-3/7 activity
comments: Complex autophagy-death crosstalk in 3D spheroids; differential responses between HCT116 and HT29 lines suggest context-dependent therapeutic strategies needed.

model_io.model: HCT116 and HT29 3D colorectal cancer colonospheres

hypotheses.hypothesis: Autophagy inhibition/activation modulates chemotherapy-induced cell death in CRC
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via differential autophagy marker and cell death pathway responses to 3-MA and CQ combinations

title: Nanopropolis mitigates cisplatin-induced submandibular gland injury by modulating oxidative stress and apoptosis
task: Determine protective mechanisms of Nanopropolis against cisplatin-induced submandibular gland injury and apoptosis
key_results: Nanopropolis (10 mg/kg/day × 14 days) substantially reversed cisplatin-induced glandular pathology: reduced collagen deposition from 29.66% to 5.72%, downregulated BAX expression, restored SOD1 mRNA from 0.223-fold to 1.042-fold near control levels, and preserved mitochondrial and ductal ultrastructure by TEM
comments: Comprehensive multimodal assessment (histology, IHC, qPCR, TEM) demonstrates robust cytoprotection; mechanism involves simultaneous oxidative stress attenuation and apoptosis suppression.

model_io.model: rat submandibular gland exposed to cisplatin

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nanopropolis mitigates cisplatin toxicity via antioxidant and anti-apoptotic mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SOD1 restoration, BAX downregulation, and architectural preservation demonstrate dual pathway protection

title: Functional alignment of protein language models via reinforcement learning
task: Aligning protein language models with experimental function via reinforcement learning for directed protein design
key_results: RLXF framework improves generation of high-functioning variants across 5 protein families; CreiLOV variants with record-high fluorescence generated via learned synergistic mutations
comments: Novel application of LLM alignment methods to protein engineering; demonstrates integration of evolutionary knowledge with experimental feedback elegantly.

hypotheses.hypothesis: RLXF-aligned models integrate evolutionary knowledge from pre-trained pLMs with experimental observations to exceed zero-shot and evolutionary baselines
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: improved generation success rates and discovery of synergistic mutations difficult to identify via traditional methods

title: Leveraging high-throughput proteomics and AI-based protein folding to accelerate VAV1 molecular glue discovery
task: Discovery and optimization of CRBN molecular glues targeting VAV1 via AI-driven structure prediction
key_results: Phenyl-glutarimide derivatives (NGT-201-12, NGT-201-18) selectively degrade VAV1 via non-canonical RT-loop degron; FEP cooperativity metrics correlate with degradation potency
comments: Integrates experimental proteomics with physics-based FEP and DFT calculations effectively; halogen substitution principle rationalization is mechanistically insightful.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-canonical RT-loop (RDxS motif) serves as VAV1 degron distinct from G-loop
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via site-directed mutagenesis and GluePlex prediction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Conformational restriction via halogen substitution potentiates CRBN-mediated degradation
hypotheses.result: Validated by SAR studies and DFT mechanistic rationalization

task: Characterizing SpoVG pleiotropic regulation of L. monocytogenes biofilm formation
key_results: SpoVG acts as dual DNA/RNA-binding protein regulating quorum sensing, chemotaxis, and PTS genes; physically interacts with cold-shock proteins and cell wall biosynthesis enzymes
comments: Comprehensive regulatory network mapping but lacks direct experimental validation of proposed anti-biofilm therapeutic strategies.

hypotheses.hypothesis: SpoVG deletion impairs biofilm formation across diverse isolates

hypotheses.hypothesis: SpoVG regulates biofilm via dual DNA/RNA-binding mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Supported by RNA-seq and protein interaction assays

title: Integrative computational analyses prioritize the host target IL15RA and the candidate compound Zafirlukast for investigation in flaviviral encephalitis
task: Systems biology prioritization of IL15RA as conserved host target and Zafirlukast as drug candidate for flaviviral encephalitis
key_results: IL15RA, IRF1, GBP1 consistently upregulated (p<0.05) across WNV/ZIKV/DENV; IL15RA predicted ligand-interaction region conserved across mammals; MD simulations support IL15RA-Zafirlukast stability (RMSD~0.35 nm)
comments: Integrated WGCNA + ML classification + cross-virus validation is rigorous; computational prioritization awaits functional validation and clinical relevance assessment.

hypotheses.hypothesis: IL15RA is a conserved host target upregulated across flaviviral infections
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: consistent upregulation in WNV, ZIKV, DENV with evolutionary conservation of ligand-interaction region

hypotheses.hypothesis: Zafirlukast favorably interacts with IL15RA and maintains complex stability
hypotheses.result: Supported by drug repurposing analysis and MD simulations (RMSD~0.35 nm)

title: Stochastic modeling for uncertainty quantification in COVID-19 dynamics using Euler Maruyama approximation
task: Uncertainty quantification in COVID-19 epidemiological dynamics using stochastic differential equations
key_results: Euler-Maruyama approximation successfully captures epidemiological data variability; extended basic reproduction number computed with uncertainty bounds
comments: Methodologically sound stochastic framework but lacks comparison with alternative uncertainty quantification approaches and real-time predictive validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stochastic perturbations in key parameters better capture observed epidemiological variability than deterministic models
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via simulation fitting to Bogotá COVID-19 data

title: First demonstration of in vivo estimation of Young’s modulus in cancers using poroelastography with experimental validation
task: In vivo estimation of tissue Young's modulus in cancers via poroelastography with Eshelby theory
key_results: Poroelastography-based Young's modulus estimation validated in murine MDA-MB-231 breast cancer with <15% error; FE/ultrasound simulations showed <5% relative error
comments: Novel application of poroelastic theory to resolve tissue compressibility limitations in elastography; first in vivo validation promising but requires translation to additional cancer models.

model_io.model: Poroelastography with Eshelby theory and lateral strain correction
outputs: Young's modulus estimates accounting for compressibility

model_io.model: Orthotopic murine MDA-MB-231 breast cancer model
outputs: ex vivo mechanical test validation (<15% error)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Poroelastic model with Eshelby correction estimates tissue Young's modulus more accurately than linearly elastic assumptions
hypotheses.result: Validated: <5% error in simulations and <15% in vivo murine tumors vs. ex vivo mechanical tests

title: Energy-aware heart disease prediction system using hybrid metaheuristic optimization and deep learning for IoT-enabled healthcare environments

key_results: SA-DNN optimized with IWOA achieved 96.7% accuracy (Cleveland), 98.56% (South African CHD), 95.05% (Framingham); ACGA clustering reduced energy consumption in simulated IoT network

comments: Addresses realistic clinical heterogeneity (modality incompleteness, non-IID distribution) but privacy guarantee for complete training transcript acknowledged as incomplete.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Modality-specific encoders with gated fusion outperform generic federated multimodal approaches under incomplete data
